trick: A bigger model reviews the code: does Opus catch more than a fresh Haiku?
source_note: Season 2 lineup (19 Oct, Showdown, headliner). Claude Code best practices: one Claude writes, a fresh Claude reviews. Three calls on both sides, same prompts: (1) Sonnet does the task; (2) a FRESH session with only Read, Grep, Glob and Bash (`--tools`, the day-15 mechanism; Bash still limited to the lab's allow list) reviews the change and lists issues in its reply, reviewer = Opus (with) or Sonnet (without); (3) a FRESH Sonnet session gets the task text and the reviewer's list ({prev_result}) and fixes what is real. Step 3 is a fresh session, not a resume of step 1: run.py resumes the latest call's session, which after step 2 is the reviewer's, so the writer's own session can't be reached without a runner change (see private/m5/SETUP_REPORT.md). Both sides carry the same Stop hook (overlay snap: tricks/d42/snap/.claude, records the repo state after every call, never blocks, prints nothing); check_step1.py grades the state after step 1, so each row also says whether the writer's first attempt already passed. Pre-registered count (behaviour_count): issues in the reviewer's list labelled by hand (tricks/d42/count_steps.py --review-step 1 --sheet) as real-bug (names a line or behaviour that a hidden test the step-1 code fails on checks) or false-alarm; nits reported, not counted. Also passes, runs fixed or broken by review+fix (count_steps.py), cost and minutes per passed task. Timeout 30 min on both sides for the three calls (days 14 and 18 precedent). Model ids must be confirmed with a one-line claude -p call before the run, as for the E1 pilot.
tasks_note: provisional; replaced by the E1 pilot's 30-70% tasks before any run. runs is per task: 9 x 2 tasks = 18 a side (headliner); with 3 tasks use 6.
model_note: Set 23 Oct after the E1 pilot: current Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 passed 20 of 20 pilot runs, so a Sonnet writer would leave nothing to review. Writer and fixer are the Season 2 model (Haiku 4.5) on both sides; the fresh reviewer is Opus 5.5 (with) vs Haiku 4.5 (without). Ids confirmed by one-line claude -p calls (runs/pilot-e1-models/models.txt).
behaviour_count: Reviewer issues hand-labelled real-bug vs false-alarm per side (real-bug = names a line or behaviour a hidden test the step-1 code fails on checks); plus runs fixed and broken by review+fix
anchor: Opus flagged N real bugs and M false alarms in 18 reviews; a fresh Haiku flagged N' and M'
